title: From the Paranormal to AI Agents: Booking.com Reveals APAC Travel Trends for 2027
excerpt: More than half of Asia-Pacific travelers are open to seeking contact with someone on the “other side,” and 70% would be interested in having an AI agent manage their work while on vacation.
content:
More than half of Asia-Pacific travelers (51%) are open to seeking contact with someone on the “other side,” according to Booking.com’s Travel Predictions 2027, and 65% are interested in paranormal travel experiences. Many also want trips that break the mold, with 75% interested in choosing a vacation specifically to do something completely out of character and 41% actively wanting to surprise their friends and family with their choices.

How travelers want to feel also weighs heavily. Some 85% of respondents in the region would choose a destination based on how they want to feel rather than where they want to go, and 83% would use a tool that recommends destinations based on their emotional state. Spending matters as well: 56% say they have reconsidered who to invite on a trip because of differences in spending, while 68% of parents are keen to travel child-free so they can spend more on themselves.

AI could also change how travelers take time off, with 70% interested in having AI cover their work while on vacation and 49% interested in using AI to catch up on missed work and take an extra day off.

“Asia-Pacific is one of the most diverse travel regions in the world, and that is reflected in how differently people are choosing to travel,” said Laura Houldsworth, Managing Director, Asia-Pacific, Booking.com.

“What we are seeing for 2027 is a stronger desire for trips that feel relevant to individual priorities, whether that is seeking new experiences, travelling with the right people or using technology to make planning simpler and more intuitive.”

Key findings

  • 75% of APAC travellers are interested in choosing a vacation specifically to do something completely out of character, with 41% actively wanting to surprise their friends and family with their choices.
  • 56% have reconsidered who to invite on a trip because of differences in spending, with 68% of parents keen to travel child-free so they can spend more on themselves.
  • 65% are interested in paranormal travel experiences, with just over half (51%) open to seeking contact with someone on the “other side”.
  • 85% would choose a destination based on how they want to feel rather than where they want to go, and 83% would use a tool that recommends destinations based on emotional state.
  • 70% would be interested in having an AI agent manage their work while on vacation and a bold 49% would use that cover to take a cheeky extra day off.

Nine Trends

Booking.com identified nine trends for 2027. Its descriptions of each trend follow, as provided by the company.

Plot Twist Trip

In 2027, travellers will humble everyone who thought they had them figured out and surprise themselves in the process with a trip nobody saw coming. Gone is “that’s not really me”, with 75% of APAC travellers interested in choosing a vacation specifically to do something completely out of character.

The reaction from others is part of the appeal, with 41% actively wanting to surprise their friends and family with their travel choices. These trips are designed to disrupt the status quo, rewrite the story everyone thought they knew, and deliver the twist nobody predicted. And for nearly a third (31%) who have deleted or avoided posting about a vacation because it felt too predictable or ordinary, this could be the year they finally have something worth sharing. The best souvenir? The look on everyone else’s face.

Social Currency

Your travel budget isn’t just deciding where you go. It’s deciding who comes with you. In 2027, budget is becoming the most ruthless filter on the guest list – and nobody is safe. More than half of APAC travellers (56%) have reconsidered who to invite on a trip because of differences in spending, while 54% have experienced tension or disagreements during a trip because people had different expectations around money.

For 43%, the solution has been even more drastic: admitting they have removed people from a travel group entirely. And for parents? The kids might not make the cut either – with 68% of parents keen to travel child-free so they can spend more on themselves. Welcome to the era of the brutally curated travel companion list. Check your bank balance. Then check the guest list.

Vibe Check(In)

Destination? Irrelevant. Vibe? Non-negotiable. In 2027, 85% of APAC travellers would choose a vacation destination primarily based on how they want to feel, rather than where they want to go. And the search filter of the future? Emotional state. More than four in five (83%) of APAC travellers would use a search tool that recommends destinations based on how they feel or their mood.

Unsurprisingly, Gen Z have entered their feels era and are ready to hand over their wearable data, phone metrics, and entire emotional state to find the right destination, with 81% of Gen Z travellers willing to share this information with a travel provider to help personalize their trip, compared to just 47% of boomers. Search by emotional intent has arrived. Mood ring, meet search filter.

The All-Exclusive

The all-inclusive buffet has served its last course. As medications reshape appetites, sobriety culture grows, and ‘macro-conscious’ eating becomes the norm, travellers are portion-controlling their vacations too. The change begins with how travellers feel about themselves, as 74% of APAC travellers say at least one health, body or lifestyle change has influenced their choice of vacation destination or activities in recent years.

And travellers no longer want to pay for what they won’t consume – the open bar they’re skipping or the buffet they’re avoiding. In 2027, less is more as 66% want a package that lets them remove services they do not expect to use. Furthermore, 66% would let their diet influence the accommodation or destination, showing that the destination now needs to fit the lifestyle. Moving forward, the most appealing travel package isn’t the one that includes everything.

Trip to the Beyond

The other side of travel is calling and in 2027, some travellers are ready to answer. While most typical trips promise sun, sea and relaxation, a growing number are seeking something altogether more unsettling: haunted histories, paranormal encounters, and the chance to sit with questions about death, memory and what might lie beyond it. The appetite for darker, more mysterious travel is on the rise, with 65% of APAC travellers interested in experiences that confront the paranormal head-on.

And for those who want to go further? Just over half (51%) would seek an experience with the hope of speaking to someone on the “other side,” while 52% are curious to take part in experiences that confront difficult questions about the afterlife, death or spirituality. Away from the rhythm of everyday life, travel creates a rare kind of openness; a chance to reflect, to remember, and for some, to feel closer to those they have lost. Turns out the most sought-after destination in 2027 isn’t a beach. It’s the beyond.

PTO: Powered by AI

The “Sunday Scaries” are checking out, thanks to AI. Nearly two-thirds (62%) of APAC travellers say the last day of vacation is less enjoyable because they are thinking about returning to work, while 42% of travellers even bring their laptop to stay on top of their inbox. AI can offer a welcome sense of relief. But do travellers trust AI enough to leave the laptop at home?

Think of it as a digital stand-in: monitoring emails, flagging priorities, sending holding responses, and keeping things ticking along while you are completely off the grid. AI could help travellers move seamlessly back into work. With 70% of travellers interested in having AI cover their work, the out-of-office could have a clever new deputy. Nearly half (47%) would be comfortable allowing AI to manage their emails and admin while away. And for the bold 49% who would ask AI to catch them up on everything they missed, there is an even sweeter upside: a cheeky extra day off, completely under the radar. Extra holidays, courtesy of artificial intelligence.

Hotel in the Sky

The flight used to be something you survived, but in 2027 it’s where the holiday starts. Wellness culture has taken over hotels, attractions, and destination experiences – now travellers want the same from 35,000 feet in the air. With 90% of APAC travellers saying they’d take a long-haul journey if it’s guaranteed they’d arrive rested and refreshed, the pressure is on to deliver.

High on the flight wish list? Food and drink menus or caffeine timing guidance designed to support sleep (37%), lighting designed to reduce jet lag (21%) and skincare kits (21%) as the bare minimum survival kit. And for a bold minority, wellness in the air goes further still. Nearly a quarter (23%) of travellers would go as far as to select a designated “no-children, quiet zone” area on board. The destination has always sold the trip, but in 2027 the flight becomes part of the getaway with travellers expecting to arrive feeling as refreshed as when they left.

Sweat Synergy

Solo travel is getting a team upgrade. In 2027, the real reason solo travellers are crossing finish lines around the world isn’t the medal, it’s who’s next to them at the end. The strongest proof of this comes from the experience, as two-thirds (66%) of APAC travellers – who have travelled alone – say a shared physical activity or challenge has led to a lasting connection or friendship.

The sport is the excuse while the connection is the reason, as 60% would be interested in joining a community of like-minded athletes or people while travelling. Shared suffering fast-tracks friendship like nothing else: the wall at kilometre 38, the post-race debrief, the group chat that never goes quiet. Next year, the 55% who are interested in travelling to attend a fitness or sporting event want more – to find friendships that go the distance.

Trailside Therapy

Move over candlelit dinners and couples massages: the new romantic getaway might be less about sex on the beach and more about tough talks with your partner. Couples aren’t just travelling to escape their problems; they may increasingly be travelling to talk about them. Almost half (49%) of APAC travellers said they would consider taking a trip to resolve conflicts or arguments, while 84% said at least one holiday activity helps them have honest or difficult conversations.

And what activity ranked among the most effective? Simply walking or hiking together (33%). This will be the year that couples take the tough conversations offsite on holiday – swapping date night for daylight, hitting the trail and letting a long walk do the talking.

The findings come from research commissioned by Booking.com and conducted in July and August 2026 among 28,230 adults planning business or leisure travel in the next 12 to 24 months. The survey covered 32 markets, including Australia, India, Japan, New Zealand, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand, and Vietnam.
